scope_note: Daily edition from matching Tuesday /new listings: 272 non-replacement cs.CV rows, 210 cs.RO rows, 455 deduplicated papers, and 382 ROI papers. Tier A cards are conservative abstract-only autopsies from repository parser output; no figure, table, full-text, code, or dataset-release claim is asserted unless the abstract itself states it.
executive_thesis: The September 22 batch is a stress test for robot decision contracts. VLA papers such as Validating, Not Sampling, LIBERO-VPro, Beyond the Leaderboard, MaskVLA, Anatomy of a Closed-Loop Collapse, and BAS-VLA show that a policy can look strong under sampled perturbations, offline validation, or nominal rollouts while failing when visual evidence becomes stale, local, task-semantic, or closed-loop. Contact papers including DexTacWAM, HapticWAM, When Does Touch Matter?, InsertAnything, and ContactDP make touch and force into correction authority rather than auxiliary features. Geometry papers including ZIL, Splat-CBF, Elevator-VIGS, WOLF, BayesianGS-SLAM, and When Wider Views Fail ask when registration, view planning, transport-state estimation, and uncertainty should change robot motion. Navigation, world-model, and safety papers then add the system rule: commitment should wait until the evidence source, action parameterization, uncertainty interval, and recovery policy are all aligned with the downstream decision.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Closed-loop robustness must be validated over regions, not sampled points
decision_cards.body: Validating, Not Sampling, LIBERO-VPro, Beyond the Leaderboard, Anatomy of a Closed-Loop Collapse, and BAS-VLA all turn robustness into a counterfactual or region-level contract rather than a nominal task score.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Touch and force are becoming action authority
decision_cards.body: DexTacWAM, HapticWAM, When Does Touch Matter?, InsertAnything, ContactDP, and ForceRFT ask which contact signal is strong enough to override or refine a vision-conditioned action.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: World models and maps need explicit evidence budgets
decision_cards.body: Splat-CBF, WOLF, BayesianGS-SLAM, OnlineWM, DualWAM, and Robot World Models Are Not Invariant to How the Actions Are Written all expose hidden contracts between observation, action encoding, uncertainty, and downstream control.

papers.title: Validating, Not Sampling: Region-Level Robustness of Vision-Language and Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.fit: VLA robustness validation - continuous perturbation regions - action sensitivity
papers.status_quo: VLM and VLA robustness is often estimated by sampling a handful of perturbed inputs.
papers.friction: A sampled pass does not certify that no nearby perturbation changes the robot decision.
papers.hidden_premise: For robot actions, robustness should be a property of an input region, not a point estimate.
papers.conceptual_move: Validate entire continuous photometric and geometric perturbation regions for VLMs and VLAs.
papers.mechanism: The abstract introduces H2V-M, a margin-aware convergence rule that searches perturbation regions efficiently at large-model scale.

evidence.claim: The paper validates brightness shifts, camera rotations, and their composition over continuous regions.
It reports that VLAs can change commanded actions under perturbations as small as plus or minus one degree.
APRL should treat camera pose and exposure perturbation regions as release gates for manipulation policies.

papers.falsification: If region-level counterexamples do not predict closed-loop failures or recoverability, the certificate is conservative but not decision-relevant.
papers.adversarial: Separate harmless action variation from contact-critical action variation; otherwise the validator can overstate risk.
papers.thinking_tool: Replace random perturbation sampling with region-level action invariance tests.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for vision-conditioned actions; less direct for policies with explicit geometric state estimation and downstream safety filters.

papers.title: LIBERO-VPro: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Visual Robustness of Robotic Foundation Models
papers.fit: closed-loop visual robustness - robotic foundation models - perturbation taxonomy
papers.status_quo: Robotic foundation models are usually tested under clean, timely, and consistent observations.
papers.friction: Nominal success can hide brittle grounding when visual evidence is degraded, stale, inconsistent, or task-relevantly changed.
papers.hidden_premise: Visual robustness is multi-dimensional and architecture-dependent, so one clean benchmark score cannot certify deployment.
papers.conceptual_move: Perturb visual evidence during closed-loop execution across degradation, staleness, source consistency, and task-relevant scene variation.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes 12 challenge categories, 96 settings, and 3,296 task-condition cases evaluated across simulated and real rollouts.

evidence.claim: The benchmark perturbs visual evidence throughout execution rather than only at the start.
The results show different robustness profiles for VLAs and WAMs.
APRL should keep stale camera, local cue disruption, and changed precondition tests separate.

papers.falsification: If perturbation families do not change model rankings or recovery choices, the benchmark may be too broad to guide design.
papers.adversarial: Real-world perturbations can co-occur; testing one axis at a time may miss coupled failures.
papers.thinking_tool: Treat visual robustness as a set of closed-loop failure families, not one corruption score.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for manipulation foundation models; needs adaptation for field robots with non-visual redundancy.

papers.title: Anatomy of a Closed-Loop Collapse: A Causal Case Study of a Compressed VLA Policy
papers.fit: compressed VLA policy - offline validation failure - closed-loop causal forensics
papers.status_quo: Compression is often accepted when offline imitation metrics or teacher ratios remain high.
papers.friction: A compressed policy can pass every offline check and still collapse to zero closed-loop success.
papers.hidden_premise: Closed-loop deployment distribution and action-trace signatures can reveal failure modes that marginal offline statistics miss.
papers.conceptual_move: Dissect one naturally occurring collapse with paired action traces, intervention tests, and deployment-distribution teacher rollouts.
papers.mechanism: The abstract isolates a late-heavy negative z residual and shows that deployment-distribution rollouts remove it and restore parity.

evidence.claim: The compressed Octo-Base student passes offline checks but scores 0/72 in the simulated closed-loop task.
A minimal-pair intervention using deployment-distribution teacher rollouts restores teacher-like behavior.
APRL should require a few dozen closed-loop trials before accepting compressed VLA policies.

papers.falsification: If the collapse signature is specific to one architecture and task, it is a case study rather than a general compression law.
papers.adversarial: Check whether the repaired policy overfits the deployment rollouts and fails under object or camera shifts.
papers.thinking_tool: Audit compression by closed-loop causal signatures, not teacher-ratio averages.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for compressed policies; less direct for safety-filtered modular controllers.

papers.title: DexTacWAM: A Visuo-Tactile World-Action Model for Dexterous Manipulation
papers.fit: visuo-tactile WAM - dexterous contact dynamics - tactile latent prediction
papers.status_quo: World-action models usually inherit video priors but remain vision-centric at deployment.
papers.friction: Dexterous contact dynamics are only partly visible, so vision-only WAMs can miss slip, force, or finger-specific contact state.
papers.hidden_premise: A tactile latent should enter the predicted world state, not merely condition an action head.
papers.conceptual_move: Encode each fingertip, compress tactile features with finger and pose awareness, and inject touch into video diffusion world modeling.
papers.mechanism: The abstract attributes gains to modeling contact evolution as part of the predicted world state rather than tactile conditioning alone.

evidence.claim: DexTacWAM models distributed multi-finger contact dynamics on a 22-DoF bimanual platform.
Removing tactile world modeling substantially lowers the reported four-task mean.
APRL should distinguish tactile feature conditioning from tactile future-state modeling.

papers.falsification: If touch improves the benchmark but does not change recovery timing or contact failure avoidance, it is predictive but not authoritative.
papers.adversarial: Evaluate unseen materials, changing fingertip calibration, and object geometries where tactile priors can overfit.
papers.thinking_tool: Make contact evolution a predicted state variable that can change action.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for tactile dexterous manipulation; weaker for grippers without reliable tactile sensing.

papers.title: HapticWAM: Distilling Imagined Touch into a World-Action Model without Inference-Time Tactile Sensing
papers.fit: tactile distillation - contact package prediction - deployment without fingertip input
papers.status_quo: Tactile sensors help contact tasks, but deployment may not support fingertip observations at inference time.
papers.friction: The policy still needs force, slip, and contact geometry estimates when direct tactile observations are unavailable.
papers.hidden_premise: A student can retain a generative contact head that imagines future contact mechanics from vision and action history.
papers.conceptual_move: Distill heterogeneous tactile contact futures and action predictions into a WAM that removes fingertip input branches at deployment.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes a teacher with gel images, deformation, shear, forces, wrench, and derived contact state, then a student with imagined touch.

evidence.claim: The model predicts a contact package, not only tactile pixels.
The student removes fingertip input branches while retaining the generative contact head.
APRL can test whether imagined touch is enough to delay, refine, or veto action chunks.

papers.falsification: If imagined touch fails exactly when contact becomes novel, the distilled representation cannot replace deployment tactile sensing.
papers.adversarial: Stress transparent, deformable, and high-friction objects where visual contact cues mislead the contact head.
papers.thinking_tool: Use tactile supervision to train a contact-state simulator that survives sensor removal.
papers.transfer_boundary: Useful for low-cost deployment; risky for high-force assembly where missing touch can cause damage.

papers.title: Splat-CBF: Safe Next-Best-View Control in 3D Gaussian-Splat Maps
papers.fit: 3D Gaussian maps - safe active perception - control barrier functions
papers.status_quo: Active perception often treats next-best-view and collision avoidance as separate planning objectives.
papers.friction: The most informative regions are often the least trusted for collision margins, so information gain can pull the robot toward unsafe space.
papers.hidden_premise: Perception should be a soft objective only after safety is encoded as a hard motion constraint.
papers.conceptual_move: Use a risk-aware CBF over Gaussian-field uncertainty for safety and a second perception barrier for expected Fisher information.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes a quadratic program where safety is hard, perception is soft, and slack adapts near uncertain regions.

evidence.claim: The method enforces collision avoidance as a hard constraint while steering toward informative views.
It reports indoor simulations and robot experiments on manipulator and Ackermann platforms.
APRL should evaluate map representations by safe information gain along the planned path.

papers.falsification: If the slack schedule frequently sacrifices perception near the very regions that matter, next-best-view gains may not reach downstream tasks.
papers.adversarial: Test dynamic obstacles and reflective clutter where Gaussian uncertainty can understate collision risk.
papers.thinking_tool: Treat view selection as a constrained control problem, not a pure reconstruction objective.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for exploration and inspection; less direct for static offline reconstruction.

papers.title: BayesianGS-SLAM: Uncertainty-Aware Neural Rendering SLAM via Probabilistic Formulation
papers.fit: uncertainty-aware GS-SLAM - predictive surprise - keyframe selection
papers.status_quo: Neural-rendering SLAM often uses rendered residuals without a consistent reliability estimate.
papers.friction: Unreliable residuals can corrupt pose optimization, while already explained frames can waste mapping updates.
papers.hidden_premise: Map representation uncertainty and sensor noise must travel through tracking, mapping, and keyframe selection together.
papers.conceptual_move: Propagate color and depth predictive uncertainty through a probabilistic 3DGS SLAM pipeline.
papers.mechanism: The abstract combines sensor-noise and opacity-induced map uncertainty and uses predictive surprise for keyframe choice.

evidence.claim: The uncertainty estimate is reused across mapping, robust pose tracking, and keyframe selection.
The keyframe strategy reduces selected keyframes and mapping calls while maintaining competitive tracking and rendering.
APRL should test whether uncertainty reduces wrong-pose commitments, not only mapping calls.

papers.falsification: If uncertainty ranks residual error but not downstream navigation risk, it remains a rendering diagnostic.
papers.adversarial: Check scene changes and dynamic objects where low predictive surprise can hide stale geometry.
papers.thinking_tool: Use predictive surprise to decide when a map update is worth trusting.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for RGB-D neural SLAM; needs adaptation for LiDAR, sonar, and event-camera pipelines.

papers.title: RiverVLN: Phase-Grounded Temporal Vision--Language Navigation for Unmanned Surface Vehicles
papers.fit: USV VLN - semantic phase tracking - continuous motion
papers.status_quo: VLN often assumes discrete indoor motion and treats language as a static goal.
papers.friction: River navigation has inertia, sparse landmarks, limited maneuverability, and long-horizon instructions that need progress state.
papers.hidden_premise: Language grounding should be converted into visually verifiable phases that can be updated online.
papers.conceptual_move: Represent navigation as phase-grounded temporal VLN with predict-execute-re-observe control for USVs.
papers.mechanism: The abstract converts instructions into ordered semantic phases and fuses phase state with visual-motion history to predict local SE(2) increments.

evidence.claim: The benchmark targets continuous riverine USV motion instead of indoor discrete actions.
PGT-NAV updates phase and grounding online and replans through a map-based safety layer.
APRL navigation benchmarks should log semantic phase progress separately from final route success.

papers.falsification: If phase labels fail under visually ambiguous bridges or currents, the representation may encode dataset landmarks rather than progress.
papers.adversarial: Stress similar-looking landmarks, current disturbances, and delayed correction after wrong phase transitions.
papers.thinking_tool: Turn long instructions into online phase commitments with re-observation gates.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for USV and long-horizon route following; less direct for short object-nav tasks.

papers.title: Robot World Models Are Not Invariant to How the Actions Are Written
papers.fit: action parameterization - world model invariance - latent rollout disagreement
papers.status_quo: Action parameterization is often treated as an implementation detail if encodings are mutually reconstructible.
papers.friction: A world model can answer a different future-prediction question when the same trajectory is written in another action coordinate system.
papers.hidden_premise: World-model invariance must be audited in the action channel, not only in visual input transformations.
papers.conceptual_move: Test whether latent dynamics are invariant to absolute versus delta action encodings and repair the defect through objective averaging and disagreement penalties.
papers.mechanism: The abstract reports large retrieval and action-selection degradation when trained and evaluated under mismatched action parameterizations.

evidence.claim: The two encodings are mutually reconstructible, yet the world model's beliefs become near-orthogonal in a PushT case.
The repair depends on where averaging is applied; output averaging is not generally available for direction-valued prediction.
APRL should treat action representation as a model contract that needs invariance tests.

papers.falsification: If controller performance is insensitive to the latent disagreement, the defect may matter more for model evaluation than deployment.
papers.adversarial: Test mixed action spaces, normalized joints, end-effector deltas, and contact-conditioned action chunks.
papers.thinking_tool: Audit the action channel as a source of hidden world-model failure.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for WAMs and imitation policies; less direct for planners with explicit dynamics models.

papers.title: BarrierFormer: Transformer-Guided Predictive Barrier Enforcement for Safe Robot Control
papers.fit: predictive safety - CBF constraints - model-free control
papers.status_quo: Standard CBF safety filters enforce constraints myopically at the current time step or require online MPC.
papers.friction: A controller can be pushed toward a future boundary where no feasible safe action remains, while online optimization can be too expensive.
papers.hidden_premise: A learned policy can internalize rollout-level barrier constraints if trained against predictive safety supervision.
papers.conceptual_move: Use a causal transformer to generate predictive rollouts, evaluate barrier violations, and learn residual corrections without online optimization.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes a dynamics head, action head, barrier critic, and safety teacher that supervises barrier-consistent actions.

evidence.claim: The method encodes rollout-level CBF constraints rather than only current-step safety.
During inference it maps observation-action history to controls without online optimization or known model dynamics.
APRL should compare predictive safety by latency, future-boundary violations, and false conservatism.

papers.falsification: If safety gains rely on simulated systems with simple dynamics, real robot deployment can reintroduce model mismatch.
papers.adversarial: Stress moving obstacles, contact-rich dynamics, and uncertainty intervals where predictive rollouts become miscalibrated.
papers.thinking_tool: Move safety from a current-step veto into a learned predictive constraint contract.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for goal-directed navigation and low-level control; needs care for high-dimensional contact manipulation.

synthesis.title: Robustness is moving from scoreboards to counterfactual contracts
synthesis.links: Validating, Not Sampling - LIBERO-VPro - Beyond the Leaderboard - BAS-VLA - Closed-Loop Collapse
synthesis.facts: The papers validate perturbation regions, closed-loop visual evidence families, edited driving scenes, task-semantic swaps, and compressed-policy rollouts.
synthesis.inference: APRL should require every policy claim to name the counterfactual that would change the action and the perturbation family that must not.

synthesis.title: Contact and geometry signals are becoming commitment gates
synthesis.links: DexTacWAM - HapticWAM - When Does Touch Matter? - Splat-CBF - BayesianGS-SLAM
synthesis.facts: The batch predicts tactile futures, compares wrench/taxel policies, enforces safe view choice, and propagates predictive uncertainty through SLAM.
synthesis.inference: The shared decision is whether an evidence source is strong enough to refine, delay, or veto a robot commitment.

synthesis.title: World-model reliability depends on hidden interface choices
synthesis.links: Robot World Models Are Not Invariant - DualWAM - OnlineWM - AffordanceWAM - DriveReferee
synthesis.facts: The papers expose action encoding, asynchronous local refinement, causal simulator queries, affordance interfaces, and analytic geometric verdicts.
synthesis.inference: APRL should audit the interface variable that links world prediction to action before judging generated futures.

frontier_memory.label: Strengthening
frontier_memory.history: September 21 emphasized early evidence timing for VLA failure, contact, mapping, social navigation, and recovery authority.
frontier_memory.body: September 22 strengthens the same axis, but shifts from first warning time to validation contracts: perturbation regions, stale evidence, tactile authority, uncertainty-aware maps, and action-encoding invariance.

frontier_memory.label: New signal
frontier_memory.history: Recent reports treated tactile WAMs and safety filters as separate lines.
frontier_memory.body: Today they converge: touch, force, barrier rollouts, conformal uncertainty, and recovery data all act as gates that decide whether a nominal command keeps authority.

frontier_memory.label: Commoditizing
frontier_memory.history: VLA, WAM, 3DGS, and Gaussian SLAM now recur almost every run.
frontier_memory.body: The differentiator is no longer proposing one of these backbones; it is proving which interface variable survives closed-loop stress and changes the robot action.

frontier_memory.label: Contradiction
frontier_memory.history: Leaderboard and nominal benchmark progress often imply that better models transfer directly.
frontier_memory.body: Counterfactual driving, closed-loop VLA collapse, LIBERO-VPro, and region validation argue that nominal success can be almost orthogonal to deployment behavior.

frontier_memory.label: Missing axis
frontier_memory.history: The repo has many per-modality diagnostics but few cross-modality arbitration rules.
frontier_memory.body: A shared arbitration benchmark is still missing: when camera, touch, map uncertainty, action encoding, and safety filter disagree, which signal should own the next command?

strategy.title: Closed-loop evidence contract benchmark
strategy.thesis: Build one suite where VLA actions are tested under perturbation regions, stale/missing camera evidence, task-semantic swaps, and compressed-policy rollout checks.
strategy.one_week: Run LIBERO-style tasks with brightness/rotation regions, camera staleness, object swap, and one compressed policy baseline.
strategy.four_week: Add driving-style counterfactual edits, action-trace residual forensics, and task-semantic calibration labels across manipulation and navigation.
strategy.success: The suite separates at least two policies that have similar nominal success but different closed-loop failure families.
strategy.stop: Stop if all axes collapse to generic confidence or clean success and do not change recovery choices.
strategy.paper_path: Benchmark paper on counterfactual closed-loop validation for robotic foundation models.
strategy.asset_path: Perturbation-region certificates, stale-camera episodes, semantic-swap labels, action traces, and recovery outcomes.
strategy.asset: Perturbation-region certificates, stale-camera episodes, semantic-swap labels, action traces, and recovery outcomes.

strategy.title: Contact authority ladder for manipulation
strategy.thesis: Rank vision, imagined touch, real tactile features, force residuals, and contact diffusion by when each should override the nominal action.
strategy.one_week: Compare vision-only, wrench, taxel, and imagined-touch signals on cluttered grasping and one insertion task.
strategy.four_week: Add DexTacWAM-style tactile world modeling, HapticWAM-style distillation, ForceRFT residual correction, and ContactDP insertion trials.
strategy.success: At least one contact channel predicts and corrects slip, jam, or force overshoot before the final failure.
strategy.stop: Stop if tactile signals improve offline prediction but cannot change recovery timing or reduce peak force.
strategy.paper_path: Manipulation paper on contact evidence as command authority for VLA/WAM policies.
strategy.asset_path: Synchronized RGB, tactile, wrench, contact package, action residual, and task-outcome logs.
strategy.asset: Synchronized RGB, tactile, wrench, contact package, action residual, and task-outcome logs.

strategy.title: Evidence-budgeted maps and world models
strategy.thesis: Audit when a robot should buy more geometry, query a simulator, trust a SLAM residual, or change the action parameterization before committing motion.
strategy.one_week: Run Splat-CBF, BayesianGS-SLAM uncertainty, and action-encoding invariance tests on one small navigation/manipulation environment.
strategy.four_week: Add ZIL registration, WOLF predictive frontiers, Elevator-VIGS transport-state stress, OnlineWM counterfactual simulator queries, and DualWAM local refinement.
strategy.success: Extra evidence or interface repair improves downstream safety or task success more than its time/compute cost.
strategy.stop: Stop if map/world-model metrics improve but route commitment, collision avoidance, or contact recovery do not.
strategy.paper_path: Systems paper on evidence budgets and hidden interface contracts in robot world models.
strategy.asset_path: View-selection logs, uncertainty maps, action-encoding pairs, simulator query traces, and downstream action changes.
strategy.asset: View-selection logs, uncertainty maps, action-encoding pairs, simulator query traces, and downstream action changes.
